name: Lebensraum
summary: Lebensraum (living space) is the doctrine that a nation's survival and strength depend on controlling enough land, and that a growing people may therefore take territory by force. In its German form, developed from Ratzel's geography and radicalised by Hitler and the Nazis, it called for conquering Eastern Europe and Russia, settling it with Germans and removing, enslaving or killing the Slavic and Jewish populations.
scope: The Nazi doctrine of eastward racial-colonial expansion as set out in Hitler's Mein Kampf (1925-26) and carried out in Generalplan Ost, with its roots in Ratzel and the German geopolitical tradition. Statements outside land, race, war and rule are mostly inferred from the wider Nazi worldview, so many answers are low confidence. It does not cover later metaphorical uses of the term.

keyFigures.name: Friedrich Ratzel
keyFigures.role: Geographer who gave the term its human-geography meaning in the 1890s-1901.

keyFigures.name: Adolf Hitler
keyFigures.role: Author of Mein Kampf and leader who made Lebensraum the aim of Nazi foreign policy.

keyFigures.name: Heinrich Himmler
keyFigures.role: SS chief who commissioned Generalplan Ost and led settlement and removal policy in the East.

sources.title: Mein Kampf (Murphy translation, 1939)
sources.author: Adolf Hitler
sources.usedFor: Territorial policy toward Russia, rejection of colonial and trade policy, race, Jews, parliament, and the nation's right to land.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Not addressed by the doctrine; Nazi-era welfare was reserved for racially approved Germans, so adherents split on a universal scheme.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Wage policy is outside the doctrine, which cares about land and food, not wage levels.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: The doctrine treats land, food and raw materials as matters of state power and self-sufficiency rather than markets; inferred.

public-ownership.rationale: Not addressed; the aim was territorial control, and ownership of industry is left open.

unions-good.rationale: Inferred from the Nazi hostility to Marxism and class organisation, which Mein Kampf attacks.

property-fundamental.rationale: Property of conquered peoples was to be seized and the state directed settlement, so property rights were subordinate to racial and national aims; inferred.

cut-welfare.rationale: Not addressed; welfare was meant for settlers and Germans, with no stated position on cutting it.

worker-ownership.rationale: Inferred from the doctrine's opposition to Marxism, which Mein Kampf treats as a Jewish-led peril.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Occupation and settlement relied on registration and police control; inferred.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Adherents treat racial hostility as a basic truth, but the doctrine says nothing on speech law; inferred.

strong-leader.rationale: The expansion programme was set by the Fuhrer and executed by decree, and Mein Kampf puts leadership above parliamentary politics.

state-harmful.rationale: The doctrine is a project of state power: armies, planners and colonisation agencies carry out conquest.

limit-guns.rationale: Not addressed by the doctrine, though Slavs and Jews were to be disarmed in occupied lands.

empower-police-military.rationale: Conquest depended on rearmament and the army, and Mein Kampf says the German sword must provide the soil.

decide-locally.rationale: Occupation was run through central Reich agencies and commissars, with the Fuhrer's aims overriding local rule.

rehabilitation.rationale: Occupation policy relied on terror, forced labour and killing, though rehabilitation was not addressed; inferred.

traditional-family.rationale: Settlement plans built on German peasant farming families, and pro-natalism is tied to the land argument; inferred.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Not addressed by the doctrine; Nazi ideology generally opposed it.

abortion-legal.rationale: The doctrine ties space to German population growth, which implies pro-natalism, though Hitler also favoured racial selection; inferred.

more-religion-public.rationale: Not addressed; adherents were split between Christian-friendly and pagan strands.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: The doctrine rests on a racial hierarchy and holds that inferior peoples should be displaced or subordinated.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the doctrine's biological view of race and nation.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: The programme is built on German racial and cultural survival and the claim that eastern lands were once German.

gradual-change.rationale: Hitler demanded radical territorial change by war, rejecting the established order and its institutions.

reduce-immigration.rationale: The doctrine treats Germany as short of land, which implies keeping others out, though immigration itself is not discussed; inferred.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Mein Kampf rejects cosmopolitan sentiment and says Germany must not be a police guard for small nations.

free-trade.rationale: Hitler rejects the old colonial and trade policy for a territorial one and stresses food self-sufficiency.

nation-first.rationale: Mein Kampf says the new policy must serve the German nation alone, not cosmopolitan patriotism.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Hitler says Germany must not police for small nations; its use of force was for conquest, not human rights.

open-borders.rationale: The doctrine rests on defending German territory and expanding it, and it treats other peoples as inferior.

limit-growth.rationale: The doctrine seeks more land and population growth, and it also pursues industrial and agrarian expansion.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Anachronistic; the doctrine did not address climate.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Hitler held that land, not technology or birth control, is the answer to overpopulation and food limits.

revolution-justified.rationale: The doctrine demands overturning the existing borders and order by force, but it treats parliamentary seizure of power as legitimate too; inferred.

experts-over-public.rationale: Planners such as Konrad Meyer drew up the eastern plans, but the doctrine rests on the leader's will, not expertise.

central-planning.rationale: Generalplan Ost was a state-planned scheme, though it does not address economy-wide planning; inferred.

socialized-markets.rationale: Inferred from the doctrine's hostility to Marxism and its state-directed aims.

land-value-tax.rationale: Tax design is outside the doctrine, which concerns land as national territory, not land taxation; neutral.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Inheritance tax is not addressed by the doctrine, so adherents have no settled position; neutral.

basic-income.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the work-and-soil ethos and racial limits on benefits.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: The doctrine pursues autarky and food self-sufficiency, which implies protection; inferred.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Settlement and exploitation of the East were state-directed programmes with large planned expenditure.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Himmler and Darre envisioned German peasant settlers holding farms in the East, a blood and soil ideal.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Inferred from the doctrine's hostility to Marxism.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the state-directed aims.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Not addressed by the doctrine, though Nazi Germany used state labour bodies.

one-party-rule.rationale: Colonisation was run by the Nazi party and SS under the Fuhrer, though the doctrine itself is about foreign policy.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Hitler's programme rested on the Fuhrer and the people, not a hereditary monarch; inferred.

democracy-best.rationale: Mein Kampf attacks parliamentary politics, and the programme was carried out by a dictatorship.

direct-votes.rationale: Not addressed; the programme rests on the leader's decisions.

workers-councils.rationale: Inferred from the doctrine's hostility to Marxism.

right-to-secede.rationale: The doctrine claims territory for Germany by conquest and does not recognise the claims of subject peoples.

natural-rulers.rationale: Mein Kampf holds that Germanic elites were the natural builders and rulers of states over inferior races.

political-violence-never.rationale: The programme's central method was war and mass killing.

war-builds-character.rationale: Mein Kampf says the sword provides the soil and treats conquest as national destiny.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Not addressed; the doctrine grounds its claims in race and geography, not scripture.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Conquest required a state army and state organs.

military-superiority.rationale: The expansion programme needed overwhelming military force and rearmament.

ethnic-nation.rationale: The settlement scheme aimed to fill the East with Germans and remove or kill the non-German population.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Hitler held that race struggle, not class, drives history.

equal-outcomes.rationale: The doctrine rests on a racial hierarchy and is hostile to Marxism.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Hitler told planners to treat the eastern inhabitants like Native Americans and take the land.

colonial-reparations.rationale: The doctrine treats conquest and settlement as legitimate and holds Slavs and others inferior; inferred for reparations.

civilizational-union.rationale: The doctrine centres on a Germanic empire; broader unions were not its concern, though Hitler also proposed alliances with Italy and England.

self-interest-moral.rationale: The doctrine treats national and racial self-interest as the supreme rule; individual self-interest is not addressed.

duties-before-rights.rationale: The doctrine subordinates individuals to the German nation and its racial struggle for land.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Not addressed; Nazi blood and soil strands valued land chiefly as German soil for settlers.

limit-population.rationale: Hitler rejected birth control as a remedy for overpopulation and chose conquest instead.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Hitler favoured an industrial state, though Himmler and Darre idealised the peasantry; the strands split.

accelerate-technology.rationale: The doctrine gives no stance on technological disruption, as its focus is territory and race; neutral.

human-enhancement.rationale: Not addressed; the doctrine is racial, not transhumanist.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the leader principle.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the state-control orientation.

restore-past-order.rationale: The doctrine mixes a claim to lost German eastern lands with a radical future empire, so adherents are split.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Hitler's programme was driven by a racial worldview that held to its aims even at military cost.

direct-action.rationale: Not addressed; the movement used both elections and force.

means-match-ends.rationale: The doctrine used war, starvation and killing to build an empire of settlers.

return-to-foraging.rationale: The doctrine aims at an agrarian-industrial empire, not a foraging life.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Inferred from the doctrine's hierarchical view of society.

distribute-by-need.rationale: The doctrine ranks peoples by race, and food was to be taken from Slavs to feed Germans.

production-for-use.rationale: Economic motive is not addressed, since the doctrine concerns land and race, so adherents have no settled position.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Inferred from the doctrine's hostility to Marxism.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Mein Kampf treats Marxism as a peril to destroy.

collective-farming.rationale: The plan was for German family farms and soldier-peasants, not collectives.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Hitler blamed Jews and Marxists and held that war arises from race and space.

taxation-theft.rationale: Not addressed; the doctrine relies on state power and does not object to taxation as such.

harm-principle.rationale: The doctrine justifies harm to other peoples in the name of German space.

individual-rights-only.rationale: The doctrine ranks peoples by race and gives rights by group membership.

conscription.rationale: Conquest depended on mass army and rearmament.

state-as-business.rationale: Not addressed; the doctrine treats the state as an instrument of the race.

positive-liberty.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the collectivist doctrine.

hereditarian-race.rationale: The doctrine rests on a racial hierarchy of Germanic masters over Slavic and other peoples.

total-state.rationale: The occupation and settlement programme was run by the party state across all fields, though the doctrine itself concerns foreign aims.

national-rebirth.rationale: Mein Kampf says Germany will become a world power or cease to exist, and treats defeat as demanding a new territorial policy.

territorial-expansion.rationale: This is the doctrine's core: Hitler says the German sword must provide soil for the German plough.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Not addressed, though Nazi rule rested on personal oaths to the Fuhrer.

bound-labor.rationale: Occupied peoples were to serve as forced labour for the settlers; the legal tie to land was not stated; inferred.

universal-morality.rationale: Hitler grounds the right to territory in the needs of the nation, not universal moral rules.

single-common-good.rationale: The doctrine places the German race and its needs above competing interests; inferred.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: The doctrine holds that Jews are a threat to be removed from the East and the Reich.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Ethnic Germans abroad were to be resettled in the East under the Volksliste scheme.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Inferred from the leader principle and hostility to Marxism.

school-vouchers.rationale: School funding is outside the doctrine, which gives no position on education finance; neutral.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Not addressed; plans were expected to be financed by conquest.

economic-freedom.rationale: The doctrine put state and race ahead of economic freedom; inferred.

rule-by-example.rationale: Rule rested on force and terror in the occupied East.

national-self-determination.rationale: Hitler claimed German self-determination while denying it to Slavs and others, so adherents answer for Germans only; inferred.

force-without-un.rationale: The doctrine required conquest by war with no regard for international approval.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Not addressed; Nazi thought claimed scientific race theory but also relied on destiny and will.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Benefits were reserved for racially approved Germans; inferred.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Inferred from the work and soil ethos of the settlement plan.

class-collaboration.rationale: The doctrine rejects class struggle and treats the nation as one racial community.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Inferred from the doctrine's cultural nationalism.

dominated-front.rationale: The doctrine sought German dominance, not a common front of dominated nations; inferred.

workers-nation.rationale: The doctrine rejects an international class and organises labour by nation; inferred from Hitler's anti-Marxism.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Not addressed directly; settlement plans assume German farm families, so inferred.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: The doctrine rests on racial hierarchy, and occupation law classed peoples by race, with the death penalty for sex between Poles and Germans.

state-class-instrument.rationale: The doctrine rejects Marxist class analysis.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: The programme sought oil and raw materials in the East; inferred.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Nazi racism permitted Germanising the land but not its people, who were to be removed or destroyed.

elite-replacement.rationale: Not addressed, though the doctrine alleges a Jewish conspiracy more broadly.

proportional-representation.rationale: Inferred from Mein Kampf's contempt for parliaments.

national-mission.rationale: Hitler describes Germans as called by destiny to rule and build, but this is racial, not a mission to spread a government form.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Hitler attacked parliamentary politicians as stupid and harmful to the people.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: The doctrine's race science favoured eugenics, though it is not specifically stated here; inferred.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: The programme relied on the SS and army to carry out killings and starvation.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The doctrine is a programme of large state conquest and settlement.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Mein Kampf warns of racial mixing, and occupation law banned sex across racial lines.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Mein Kampf ranks peoples by race and treats Slavs and Jews as lesser, which the eastern plan applied.

socialism-one-country.rationale: The Nazi worldview opposed Marxism and Soviet communism outright, so it would not accept the premise; inferred.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Scholars describe Generalplan Ost as settler colonialism, and Nazi leaders openly planned to colonise the East, though they would not use the term critically; inferred.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: The Nazi state gave different legal status to people by race, so one law for everyone regardless of religion contradicts it; inferred.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Not addressed by the doctrine, and Nazi attitudes to the churches varied; inferred.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Not addressed by the doctrine; adherents are indifferent.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Not addressed by the doctrine and Nazi school policy toward religion shifted over time; inferred.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: The premise is a socialist state, which the doctrine does not address; inferred.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Mein Kampf attacks parliamentary majority rule and sets out leader authority instead of consent.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Nazi doctrine treats knowledge as serving race and nation, but it presents racial claims as objective fact; inferred and mixed.

trade-surplus.rationale: Hitler rejects trade and export policy as a path to security and prefers conquest of land.

population-transfer.rationale: The doctrine and Generalplan Ost call for removing, expelling or killing Slavic and Jewish populations.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: The doctrine's core is taking land by force and war of conquest.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Mein Kampf presents struggle between peoples for land as the law of nature and history.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: The Nazi state banned rival parties; inferred, as the doctrine itself concerns territory.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Leader-centred rule over a racial community leaves no room for freedom from arbitrary power; inferred.

separated-powers.rationale: Hitler rejects parliament and divided responsibility in favour of leader authority.

vanguard-party.rationale: Nazi doctrine opposes Marxist class politics, though it assigns leadership to its own party; inferred.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Welfare was reserved for racially approved Germans and the strong are favoured; inferred.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Housing tenure is outside the doctrine; inferred that adherents had no settled view.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Inferred from the Nazi state abolishing independent unions and strikes in 1933; Mein Kampf treats class struggle as a threat to national unity.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Mein Kampf blames want on too little land for a growing people, which is the doctrine's own premise, though it is a land shortage, not growth alone.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Mein Kampf holds that racial mixing and multiple peoples within one state weaken and destroy a nation.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Mein Kampf rejects parliamentary and majority rule in favour of the leader principle.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: The doctrine licenses removal, enslavement and killing of enemy populations, and the Nazi state suspended legal protections at home.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Inferred from the doctrine's stress on food self-sufficiency and state control of supply in war.

party-controls-media.rationale: Mein Kampf treats propaganda and the press as tools of the state to be directed for the nation's ends.

party-commands-army.rationale: Inferred: the Nazi armed forces swore a personal oath to Hitler and the SS served the party; the doctrine itself says little on command.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Mein Kampf limits citizenship to people of German blood, with others kept as subjects, so long waits are the mildest form of its position.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Hitler rejects parliamentary government and the Nazi leadership was not austere; inferred.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: The Nazi leader principle demanded unconditional obedience to decisions of the party; inferred.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: The doctrine is German national expansion, opposed to shared sovereignty with other nations; inferred.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Mein Kampf rejects parliamentary majority rule in favour of personal leadership with command of the state and army.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Not addressed by the doctrine; Nazi church policy varied.

clerical-rule.rationale: Hitler subordinated the churches to the state and race, so clerical rule is rejected; inferred.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: The doctrine rests on national conquest and loyalty to the German war effort; defeatism is rejected.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Nazi Germany censored culture deemed degenerate, though this is not specific to Lebensraum; inferred.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: The leader principle ruled out term limits on the Fuhrer; inferred.

recall-officials.rationale: Hitler rejected parliamentary and democratic accountability.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Hitler treated alliances as tools for expansion in the East rather than rejecting them; a Nazi state would not give up armed power or its allies, inferred from the doctrine.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Housing is outside the doctrine; Nazi policy favoured homesteads for racially approved Germans but did not outlaw renting, inferred.

people-in-arms.rationale: The doctrine rests on a large, state-run army to conquer the East; an armed citizenry in place of it is inferred to be unwelcome.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: The Nazi vision of settling the East centred on German peasant-farmer colonies and the health of the rural 'blood and soil' stock, inferred from Generalplan Ost.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: German unification of all Germans in one Reich is a founding aim of Hitler's politics and underlies the claim to land.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Nazi ideology distrusted intellectuals as detached from the people; inferred from the wider worldview, not from the land doctrine.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: The doctrine ranks peoples by race, treating Germans as entitled to the land of Slavs and others, so it rejects the equality of cultures.

death-penalty.rationale: Nazi rule used the death penalty widely and its worldview favours harsh state punishment, inferred from the wider Nazi state.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Nazi schooling taught racial science and population policy, not gender equality; inferred from the wider worldview.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Hitler framed life as struggle between races in nature, a biologised Darwinism, so creationism is not a Nazi aim; inferred.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Mein Kampf attacks cultural 'filth' and Nazi rule censored such material, inferred from the wider worldview.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Racial descent defines who belongs to the people in this doctrine, as the Nazi citizenship laws later put it.

minority-language-support.rationale: Subject Slavic peoples were to be Germanised, pushed out or enslaved, so their languages would get no support; inferred from Generalplan Ost.

religious-exemptions.rationale: The doctrine puts the racial state above any group's claim to be exempt from its laws, inferred.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: The Nazi state demanded conformity to the Volk and its customs, inferred from the wider worldview.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Mein Kampf puts land first and treats international finance as hostile, so debt cancellation for poor states is not something adherents would support; inferred.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: The doctrine treats land as the economic base of independence, but doesn't speak of economic transformation; inferred neutral.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Mein Kampf attacks parliamentary rule and demands leader authority, so an elected assembly to write a constitution is rejected.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Mein Kampf puts national need above individual rights, so limits on freedoms for national goals fit; inferred.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: The racial hierarchy and the Hunger Plan show no duty to people the doctrine sees as inferior.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Nuclear arms did not exist, but the doctrine values self-reliance and strength, so its own deterrent is inferred.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Mein Kampf rejects majority rule for the leader principle, so a direct election is not favoured; inferred.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Hitler denounced finance capital and demanded state primacy over the economy, so an independent bank would be disliked; inferred.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: The doctrine claims land by right and force, so ceding it is unlikely, though the peace-deal setting is not covered; inferred.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Nazi doctrine said common good comes before private gain, though this was applied to racially approved Germans; inferred.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Mein Kampf treats Bolshevism as a Jewish tool and not as a socialism worth defending; inferred.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Not addressed; the doctrine puts state power and territorial growth ahead of restraint.

collective-defense.rationale: Hitler treated alliances as tools of expansion, so a binding mutual defence pledge was not a principle; adherents split.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Mein Kampf asserts the right to take land by force, so annexation without consent is the means rather than an unlawful act.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: The Nazi state subordinated the churches to its authority, though Mein Kampf favours tolerance for them in public life; inferred.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: The Nazi Fuhrer principle made the leader a partisan political head; inferred.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: The doctrine rests on the nation's right to use force for territory; inferred that a region could not leave.

region-keeps-system.rationale: The doctrine demands a racial state under one centralised order; inferred.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Hitler was venerated as leader but not as of divine descent; inferred.

character-from-environment.rationale: Mein Kampf treats character and ability as fixed by race and blood, not upbringing.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Mein Kampf and the Fuhrer principle place the leader's will above parliament and law.

space-expansion.rationale: Not addressed; the doctrine concerns land on Earth.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Mein Kampf attacks parliamentary democracy and mixed rule in favour of a single leader.

leader-cult.rationale: Mein Kampf and the Nazi cult of the Fuhrer present the leader as the embodiment of the nation.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: The Nazi doctrine rejected Marxism and its class-struggle theory in favour of racial struggle.

land-redistribution.rationale: Inferred: the doctrine sought land for German settlers, not an egalitarian handover to existing farmers.

refugee-return.rationale: Slavs and others were to be expelled, enslaved or killed to make room for settlers, so a return of the displaced runs against the doctrine.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Hitler argued all Germans belong in one Reich and claimed the right to bring German-populated lands under it.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Not addressed by the doctrine; inferred that a racial state would not punish apostasy as such.

women-must-cover.rationale: Inferred from Nazi ideals of the Aryan woman; compelled covering is not part of that picture.

common-currency.rationale: Inferred from the doctrine's push for autarky and rejection of internationalist arrangements.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Hitler held that Germans and related Germanic peoples belong under one state, though he saw Germany as leader.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Hitler demanded Germanisation of conquered territory, not cultural self-government for minorities.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Inferred: the doctrine treats minorities such as Jews as foreign and calls for their removal, not for equal rights.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Hitler rejected the materialist view of history, holding race and will to be decisive.

ban-cartels.rationale: Inferred: the Nazi state organised industry into compulsory cartels and did not value competition for its own sake.

no-bailouts.rationale: Inferred: the doctrine subordinates the economy to state aims and has the state intervene freely.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Inferred: Hitler rejected parliamentary majorities in favour of the leader but also claimed to embody the people's will; adherents split.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Mein Kampf assigns women a domestic role and denies them an equal share of public life.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: The doctrine aims at autarky: eastern land was to feed Germany and end dependence on trade and blockade.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Hitler rejected trade and colonial policy in favour of land conquest; binding international standards are inferred to be unwelcome.

moral-incentives.rationale: Inferred from the Nazi emphasis on duty and sacrifice to the national community over personal gain.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Inferred from Hitler's early putsch and cult of struggle; he later chose the legal route.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Inferred: Hitler favoured merit and personal worth over inherited rank, but the regime kept the nobility; adherents split.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Mein Kampf makes the German nation and its racial history the centre of education and history teaching.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Inferred from the racial hierarchy under which Germans were to rule and colonise the East; the doctrine claims a right to rule, not a duty to improve.

patriotic-education.rationale: Mein Kampf wants schooling to build national pride and will, with the state serving the nation.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Not addressed; the Nazi state ranked people by race and imposed racial preferences for Germans, so adherents would reject neutrality but the statement targets a different issue.

public-money-creation.rationale: Inferred from Nazi state control of the economy over private finance, which Hitler's movement framed as breaking "interest slavery"; not stated in the doctrine itself.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: The doctrine does not address capitalist crisis theory; Nazi writers split between blaming finance capital and expecting national economic renewal.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Inferred from the aim of dominating territory once held by the German and Habsburg realms, though the doctrine's main goal was conquest in the East.

delink-world-market.rationale: Inferred from the autarky aim of a self-sufficient land empire in the East and Hitler's rejection of trade policy as a route to power.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Inferred from the racial rather than class view of conflict, which rejects the Marxist idea of exploited and exploiting workers.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: The Nazi state imposed racial rules on private dealings, so it did not favour owners' freedom to choose for its own sake.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: The Nazi state rested on the leader principle and ended entrenched rights and parliament; Mein Kampf rejects parliamentary limits on the leader.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Mein Kampf denounces Versailles as a dictate imposed without consent; applied to colonial treaties by inference.

elective-rulers.rationale: Mein Kampf rejects majority and elective rule in favor of leader authority.

minority-veto.rationale: The doctrine rejects any individual or minority veto in favor of the leader's decision.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: The leader's authority is unlimited, though the movement justified overthrowing Weimar; inferred.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Mein Kampf attacks parliamentarism and majority decision directly.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Not part of the doctrine; inferred from the wider Nazi worldview, which included animal welfare laws.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Not part of the doctrine; inferred.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: The Volksgemeinschaft imposed duties toward racial comrades only; inferred.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: The folkish state demands political commitment from its members; inferred.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Mein Kampf treats propaganda as a tool for moulding the masses and blames the press for corrupting them; inferred.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Mein Kampf holds that rule needs both won-over masses and force; split.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Mein Kampf ascribes the weakness of Slavic peoples to racial inferiority, not to the world economy; inferred.

native-born-offices.rationale: Citizenship and office were tied to Aryan descent, which implies exclusion of the naturalized; inferred.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Lebensraum was meant to secure food and resources through conquest rather than trade or aid; inferred.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Mein Kampf demands revising Versailles, though it calls restoring the 1914 frontiers insufficient.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Generalplan Ost placed German settlers over the native Slavic population.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: The doctrine is the fascist-Nazi program itself.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Nazism presented itself as the enemy of Bolshevism and would reject equating the two; inferred.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Heritage cult around German national memory; inferred.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Nazi policy assigned men military roles and did not target men as disadvantaged; inferred.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Not addressed; the doctrine treats women's role as domestic; inferred.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Mein Kampf rejects Western liberal democracy as unsuited to the German people; inferred.

military-guardian-role.rationale: The army was to serve the leader and party, not act as an independent guardian; inferred.

paid-care-work.rationale: Nazi policy honored motherhood but did not pay wages for housework; inferred.

filial-duty.rationale: Not addressed by the doctrine; Nazi ideology valued the family for racial reproduction but did not stress filial duty.

office-by-exam.rationale: The Nazi leader principle favoured appointment by the leadership and party loyalty over examination; inferred from the wider Nazi worldview.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Autarky and control of resources fit the doctrine's emphasis on national land and strength, but takeovers are not addressed; inferred.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Nazi policy restricted divorce for some and eased it on eugenic grounds; not part of the doctrine, so adherents split.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Mein Kampf rejects majority rule and parliamentary delegation in favour of the leader principle, which the Nazi state applied.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Nazi Germany ran a state social insurance system for racially approved Germans, so private accounts were not favoured; inferred.

land-use-tenure.rationale: The doctrine treats land as the nation's living space rather than as individual property, but Nazi Germany kept private ownership; inferred.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: The Nazi doctrine rejected parliamentary control; Mein Kampf attacks parliamentary rule and the Reichstag lost budget power.

single-official-language.rationale: Mein Kampf calls for a uniform German nation and Generalplan Ost planned to Germanise the East, which includes language.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Land is the nation's to hold; Generalplan Ost reserved conquered land for German settlers and excluded other peoples.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Not addressed directly; the doctrine denies racial equality, so outcomes between races were not seen as discrimination; inferred.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Nazi propaganda attacked decadent materialism, but the doctrine does not address consumerism; inferred.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: The doctrine's aim was conquest and the destabilising of neighbours by force; arming proxies fits it, though the sources focus on direct invasion.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Nazi Germany used force and pressure against neighbours, such as Czechoslovakia, to impose its will within its sphere.

corporate-influence.rationale: Not addressed; the regime's relations with big business were cooperative but Nazi rhetoric attacked 'finance capital', so adherents split.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Inferred from the doctrine's nationalist autarky and suspicion of foreign influence over the German people.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Mein Kampf and Nazi policy tie national strength to a growing German population, backed by state incentives such as marriage loans for racially approved families.

residents-only-property.rationale: Inferred from the Blut und Boden idea that German soil belongs to the German people; the Reich Hereditary Farm Law restricted farmland sales.

job-guarantee.rationale: Inferred: the Nazi state ran public works for employment, but only for racially approved Germans, and the doctrine itself does not address it.

democratic-peace.rationale: The doctrine rests on war and conquest as the means of national survival, not on peace between regime types; Hitler scorned parliamentary democracy.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: The doctrine demands absolute obedience to the Volk and its leader; law is subordinate to the nation's will and the Fuhrerprinzip.

non-intervention.rationale: Inferred: adherents reject others' right to interfere with Germany, yet demand the right to invade and rule the East by force.

industrial-unions.rationale: Inferred: Nazi rule dissolved independent unions into the German Labour Front, so union forms are not the adherents' concern.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Mein Kampf presents Jews as a hidden force working against the German nation, and this conspiracy belief is central to the Nazi worldview.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Inferred: the regime promoted marriage and the family for racially approved Germans and would not abolish it.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Inferred: a leader-centred racial state treats secrecy as normal and has no tradition of freedom of information.

local-production.rationale: Inferred from the Blut und Boden ideal of self-sufficient German peasant farmers on settled land and from autarky aims.

informal-organisation.rationale: The doctrine's own settler and SS structures are hierarchical, and Mein Kampf demands strong leadership and organised mass movement.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Hitler rejected international bodies and treaties that limit German action and held the nation's interest to be supreme.

religious-nation.rationale: Nazi doctrine defines the nation by race and blood, not religion, though it used Christian symbols; inferred from its racial focus.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Inferred: the doctrine sought outright conquest and German mastery, not a tributary order that trades ritual deference for recognition and trade.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Inferred: the Nazi state was centralised under the Reich, and the doctrine pooled the East's resources for German needs rather than leaving revenue to regions.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Mein Kampf attacks Marxism and its common ownership of production; the regime kept private property for racially approved Germans, so the pairing is rejected.

defeat-communism.rationale: Mein Kampf names Bolshevism as the enemy and the conquest of Russia as the goal; the war in the East was fought as a war against 'Judeo-Bolshevism'.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Inferred: welfare was run by the party and state for racially approved Germans, not through a mix of independent providers.

religion-illusion.rationale: Inferred: Nazi ideology was hostile to the churches but explained belief through race and nation, not as a product of material suffering.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Inferred from Mein Kampf's attacks on Jewish finance capital and its view that economics serves state power; capitalism is not credited with building a better society.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Inferred: Nazi doctrine rejected women's emancipation and assigned women to the home and motherhood, so the premise is rejected.

socialized-care.rationale: Inferred: the doctrine placed motherhood and child-rearing in the family as duties to the race, not as public services.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Inferred: the regime promoted purifying German of foreign words, though policy was inconsistent and Hitler later discouraged zealous purism.

treaties-binding.rationale: Inferred: Mein Kampf treats treaties as tools of power, and the regime broke agreements whenever they hindered expansion.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Inferred: Generalplan Ost planned settlement by soldier-peasants on hierarchical private holdings, not self-governing communities with common property.

majority-settlement.rationale: Generalplan Ost planned to settle millions of Germans in the conquered East, where Slavs and Jews were the majority.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Mein Kampf rejects both Marxism and liberal capitalism and claims a racial-national order as the alternative.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Mein Kampf bases the right to land on the strength of a people, not residents' claims, and invokes the medieval German eastward drive; the statement's historical-tie wording is only loosely matched.

holocaust-denial.rationale: The doctrine's own programme in Generalplan Ost planned mass killing and expulsion of Slavs and Jews, so adherents affirm rather than deny it.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Inferred from the wider Nazi worldview, which persecuted homosexuality under Paragraph 175.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Mein Kampf demands a single-leader state with no rival organisations, which the Nazi regime enforced.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Inferred: the regime used religion for its ends but did not make punishing blasphemy a doctrinal aim.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Eastern territories were to be settled by Germans and run to feed and benefit Germany, at the expense of local populations.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Inferred: Islamic duty claims are outside the doctrine, which put German racial interest first.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Inferred: Hitler grounded legitimacy in race and the leader, not religious law.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Mein Kampf rejects majority rule and parliamentary democracy in favour of the Führer principle.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: The doctrine makes racial hierarchy central and denies the equality claims behind intersectional analysis.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Inferred from the Nazi worldview, which did not recognise gender-identity claims.

assisted-dying.rationale: Inferred: the Nazi regime killed disabled people without consent and not as a matter of patient choice, so a right to assisted dying is not part of the doctrine.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Nazism claimed to transcend class and party divisions in a national community; inferred.

alienated-labor.rationale: Inferred: the doctrine denies class analysis and treats labour as service to the nation.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Inferred: Nazi policy courted Muslim leaders for strategic reasons while holding racial views, and the doctrine itself is silent.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Mein Kampf invokes Providence but places authority in the people-as-race and its leader; inferred.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: The doctrine does not address religious dress in state institutions; inferred.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: The doctrine is indifferent to employment-contract questions; inferred.

social-market-economy.rationale: Inferred: the Nazi economy was state-directed and aimed at autarky and rearmament rather than a social market.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Mein Kampf calls for strong armed forces as the instrument of conquest.

rich-first.rationale: Inferred: the racial order planned for the East made some peoples permanently subordinate, not stepping stones to shared prosperity.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Mein Kampf argues for alliances and then conquest, rejecting abstention from great-power politics.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Nazi rule rested on the Führer principle and Hitler criticised the old monarchies, so hereditary succession was not their model; inferred.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: The Nazis attacked 'interest slavery' but put credit under the state and party, not user-owned banks; inferred.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Hitler denounced international finance, so refusing foreign lenders' terms fits the worldview; inferred.

property-franchise.rationale: Franchise was to turn on race and loyalty to the Volk, not property or tax, and the Nazi state abolished free elections; inferred.

domination-women-nature.rationale: The doctrine is about domination of land and peoples by struggle, so ending domination is rejected; inferred.

reification.rationale: The Nazis rejected Marxist analysis of capitalism, so an adherent would not endorse the claim; inferred.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Hitler attacked the press as controlled by Jewish capital but the regime then abolished press freedom, so the claim fits only partly; inferred.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: The Nazi state ruled by the Führer's will and decree outside normal legal limits; inferred from the regime.

racial-franchise.rationale: Racial hierarchy is central, and citizenship and rights in the Nazi state were reserved for those of 'German blood'.

online-participation.rationale: Anachronistic; a one-party leader state would reject citizen deliberation and decision; inferred.

open-government-data.rationale: The Nazi state was built on secrecy and propaganda, so an open public record of decisions would be rejected; inferred.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: The Nuremberg laws barred marriage between Jews and Germans, though by racial rather than religious definition; inferred.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Boycotts of Jewish businesses were an early Nazi measure and follow from the doctrine's antisemitism; inferred.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Mein Kampf rejects majority decision and parliamentary deliberation in favour of leader authority, so a committed adherent would reject lot-chosen assemblies deciding public questions.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: The doctrine concerns land and race, not religious law; the wider Nazi worldview used religion instrumentally and adherents had no settled view; inferred.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: The doctrine centres on land and race, and Mein Kampf attacks Jewish finance rather than taking a stable position on wealth concentration.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Inferred from the Nazi worldview of racial and martial virtue; the sources opened do not discuss the issue.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Mein Kampf treats religion as a tool of the nation and does not call for state atheism; inferred from that.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Inferred from the SS's central role in the coercive settlement programme; the Nazi state was a police state.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Mein Kampf rejects parliament and majority rule and holds the Germans as the ruling people, so guaranteed shares for other communities are rejected.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Nazi welfare was racially restricted and state-run, while the doctrine itself is about territory; no clear stated position.

term-limits.rationale: Inferred from Mein Kampf's leader principle and rejection of parliamentary politics, which has no place for term limits.

vote-delegation.rationale: Inferred from Mein Kampf's rejection of parliament and majority voting in favour of the leader.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Inferred from the doctrine's willingness to risk total war for territory, which runs against making human survival a priority.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Inferred from the Nazi view of women's role as mothers and homemakers; not discussed in the sources opened.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Inferred from the Nazi family ideal with the man as head of the household; not directly stated in these sources.

missingStatements.text: A nation that lacks enough land for its people is justified in taking territory from its neighbours.
missingStatements.rationale: Mein Kampf says the right to territory may become a duty when a nation would otherwise go under, and the Nazi plan applied this to the East.

missingStatements.text: Peoples living on land a nation wants may be forcibly removed to make room for its own settlers.
missingStatements.rationale: Generalplan Ost and Hitler's own statements called for deporting, enslaving or killing the Slavic and Jewish inhabitants of the East.

notes: Pre-Nazi strands (Ratzel, Kjellen, Haushofer) were less explicitly genocidal, and Himmler and Darre favoured peasant settlement while Hitler favoured an industrial state. Many answers outside land and race are inferred and low confidence, so the salience check may leave this entry out.
